# `ecommerce_order_status_valid`

> The status must be a step of the order lifecycle: placed, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled or refunded.

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain | [ecommerce](README.md) |
| Layer | **silver** — evaluated by the `silver` gate |
| Model | `slv_ecommerce__orders` (`ecommerce_silver.slv_ecommerce__orders`) |
| Column | `status` |
| Check | `accepted_values` |
| Severity | `error` — a violation **stops the pipeline** |
| Defined in | [dbt/models/ecommerce/silver/_silver.yml](../../../dbt/models/ecommerce/silver/_silver.yml) |

## What it checks

`status` is one of: `placed`, `paid`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, `refunded`.

## When it fails

The `silver` task of `medallion_ecommerce` fails, gold and `publish_gold` don't run, and the batch is never added to `ecommerce_gold`: consumers keep the batches published before. `quality_report` marks the run as blocked and sends the alert, if one is configured.

The rows that broke the rule in its latest evaluation are kept in `dq_audit.ecommerce_order_status_valid`.

## Tested by

Scenario **`invalid_order_status`**: order status outside the order lifecycle.

```bash
make generate DOMAIN=ecommerce SCENARIO=invalid_order_status BATCH=2026-10-20_invalid_order_status
make pipeline DOMAIN=ecommerce BATCH=2026-10-20_invalid_order_status
```
